facts.fact: Pass 10+2 with Physics and Mathematics compulsory plus Chemistry or Biotechnology/Biology/Technical Vocational/Computer Science/IT/Informatics Practices/Agriculture/Engineering Graphics/Business Studies/Electronics/Entrepreneurship, and appear in all PCM papers of MHT-CET 2026 with a non-zero score (Appendix 5 of the 2026 brochure, which says criteria are carried from the 2025-26 brochure).
At least 45% in the qualifying subjects taken together (Open); at least 40% for Reserved categories, EWS and PwD candidates belonging to the Maharashtra State only.

Physics and Chemistry compulsory plus Maths/Biology/etc. with the same 45%/40% rule and a non-zero MHT-CET PCB score qualifies only for nine disciplines: Agriculture Engg, Biotechnology, Food Engg, Leather, Packaging, Pharmaceutical Engg, Printing, Fashion Technology, Textile Chemistry.

facts.topic: Role of Class 12 marks in merit
facts.fact: Merit for B.E./B.Tech is prepared on MHT-CET (or other designated entrance) score; Class 12 marks are used for the eligibility cut-off and only as tie-breakers (CET Maths, Physics, Chemistry, then PCM % at board, then Maths %, Physics %, aggregate %). No Class 12 weightage or normalisation is stated in the merit rule.
Percentage is rounded to the nearest integer (44.50 to 44.99 counts as 45); if a candidate reappears in all subjects, the latest marks are used.
Their merit list uses the percentage in Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics at the qualifying exam, not CET.

Type A: SSC and HSC (or equivalent) from Maharashtra, or domicile of Maharashtra and/or born in Maharashtra; Type B: parent domiciled in Maharashtra with certificate; Type C: parent a Government of India or its undertaking employee posted in Maharashtra; Type D: parent employee or retired employee of Govt of Maharashtra or its undertaking; Type E: Maharashtra-Karnataka border area candidates with Marathi mother tongue.

Indian nationals not claiming Maharashtra State candidature are All India candidates; for B.E./B.Tech they need a non-zero JEE (Main) score or non-zero MHT-CET PCM score, with JEE (Main) preferred over MHT-CET; same 45% Class 12 rule (40% concession worded for Maharashtra State reserved/EWS/PwD).

MHT-CET 2026 is mandatory for Maharashtra State and Minority candidates seeking B.E./B.Tech and B.Pharm/Pharm.D; All India candidates may use JEE (Main) for B.E./B.Tech and NEET for B.Pharm/Pharm.D, which is preferred over MHT-CET.
No age limit for appearing in MHT-CET 2026 or for admission; candidates passed or appearing in HSC/12th with Indian nationality may appear.

10+2 with English and Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics/Biology as optional subjects, non-zero MHT-CET score (Maharashtra) or non-zero NEET/MHT-CET score (All India); the 2026 brochure states no minimum percentage; NIOS/open-school 10+2 is not eligible.
10+2 with Physics and Chemistry compulsory plus Mathematics or Biology (or D.Pharm), non-zero MHT-CET score (Maharashtra) or non-zero NEET/MHT-CET score (All India); no minimum percentage stated.

Indian national with Class 12 Science with not less than 45% (General/Open) and 40% in aggregate for Reserved (SC/ST, VJ-A, NT-B/C/D, OBC, SBC, SEBC, EWS) and physically handicapped candidates; entrance via MHT-CET, JEE, NEET or ICAR AIEEA-UG, with merit including other weightages notified by the Government of Maharashtra.

Maharashtra State (MS) candidature: Maharashtra domicile, or school leaving certificate/birth certificate showing birth in Maharashtra; Other State (OMS) candidature: domicile/residence certificate from another state.

State Common Entrance Test Cell, Maharashtra is the Competent Authority for MBBS/BDS state quota CAP on NEET (UG) 2026 merit; separate state registration is mandatory even if registered for All India Quota counselling.
Revised round 1: registration extended to 15/08/2026, provisional merit list 18/08, final merit list and seat matrix 21/08, choice filling 22-24/08, allotment 25/08, joining 26-30/08/2026.
NRI candidates are eligible only for the 15% Institute Quota as per merit and register on the Foreign Candidate Registration Portal.
PwD candidates must have claimed the quota at NEET 2026 and submit a certificate from a listed medical board; EWS must be in the Maharashtra Government format valid for 2026-27.

Open and EWS: not less than 50% (150/300) in Physics, Chemistry, Biology at HSC; constitutional reservation and SEBC (including with PwD): 40% (120/300); General-category PwD: 45% (135/300) or as decided by the central council. This is the 2025-26 brochure; the 2026-27 NEET brochure was not retrievable.
Not less than 50 percentile in NEET PCB for Open/EWS; 40 percentile for constitutional reservation/SEBC (with or without PwD); 45 percentile for General PwD.

facts.topic: MBBS/BDS domicile and school rule (2025-26 brochure)
facts.fact: Candidate must be domicile of Maharashtra (with listed exceptions such as defence personnel and central government employees' children), must have passed SSC and HSC from Maharashtra institutions with English, Physics, Chemistry and Biology (limited exemptions), and born on or before 31 Dec 2008 for the 2025 cycle.

On the CET Cell home page only a paper-setter invitation for MAH-CET A.Y. 2027-28 (02/10/2026) was seen; no MHT-CET 2027 brochure, dates or eligibility were published as of 5 Nov 2026, and the CAP brochure page lists no 2027-28 brochure.
For All India candidates, JEE (Main) 2026 score is preferred over MHT-CET for B.E./B.Tech; for pharmacy, NEET is preferred.

GGSIPU B.Tech (Code 131, admission by JEE Main Paper 1 rank; the university runs no CET for it) needs Class 12 with at least 55% aggregate in Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics, passed in each subject separately, plus a pass in English.

For these majors the 55% aggregate applies to Physics and Mathematics (mandatory) plus one other listed subject (Chemistry, Computer Science, Electronics, IT, Biology, etc.), each passed separately; candidates must also check the AICTE handbook 2026-27.
The brochure says reserved-category relaxation of marks is 'as per the University policy' and the pages read do not state a figure for SC/ST/OBC/PwD in B.Tech.
B.Tech seats go by merit/rank in JEE Main Paper 1; the university does not hold its own CET for them; blind, colour-blind, deaf or dumb candidates are not eligible.

Delhi Region = 85% of sanctioned intake for candidates who passed the qualifying exam from a school/institute located in NCT of Delhi (or a college affiliated to GGSIPU); Outside Delhi Region = 15% for those who passed it from outside Delhi, even if they live in Delhi; domicile or residence does not decide it.
A candidate who passed through distance/open schooling counts as Delhi Region only if the study centre is in Delhi and the candidate proves it.

In University Schools and Govt institutes the Delhi 85% carries DSC 15%, DST 7.5%, DOBC 27%, Defence 5%, PwD 5%; the outside-Delhi 15% carries SC 15%, ST 7.5%, Defence 5%, PwD 5%; self-financing colleges also hold 10% management quota.
For UG programmes with a 12th-pass entry (other than MBBS) a candidate should not be beyond 21 years on 01.08.2026, relaxable by up to 5 years in exceptional cases on written application.

The brochure entry for B.Pharm (Code 133) asks for 10+2 with English and Physics, Chemistry and Maths and/or Biology as individual subjects, as per Pharmacy Council of India norms; a minimum-marks figure is not stated on the page.

B.Sc (Hons) Nursing (Code 115, unmarried female candidates only) needs Class 12 Science with at least 45% in Physics, Chemistry and Biology taken together and a pass in English; admission is on NEET UG 2026 merit first, then CET.
BPT/BOT (Code 119) needs at least 50% aggregate in Physics, Chemistry and Biology, passed in each subject, plus English; admission is on NEET UG 2026 merit.
At reporting, MBBS/BAMS/BHMS candidates must show 50% or more in aggregate in Physics, Chemistry and Biology/Biotechnology (40% for SC/ST) with a pass in English, plus the NEET score card.
MBBS/BAMS/BHMS candidates must be at least 17 years on or before 31 December of the admission year, with a 25-year upper limit and 5 years' relaxation for SC/ST/OBC.
The GGSIPU brochure says BDS admissions may be carried out by DGHS, Govt of India (central counselling by the Medical Counselling Committee), so candidates need not apply in GGSIPU.
GGSIPU posted an MBBS (Code 103) special stray round notice dated 05.11.2026 and a B.Sc (H) Nursing (Code 115) extended stray round dated 02.11.2026, so the 2026 NEET counselling is still running.

facts.topic: JAC Delhi for DTU, NSUT, IIIT Delhi
facts.fact: B.Tech at NSUT, DTU, IGDTUW, IIIT-Delhi and DSEU is filled through JAC Delhi (Joint Admission Committee, run online with NIC support) on JEE Main rank, not through JoSAA; 7,765 engineering seats in 2026.

85% of seats in every participating institute go to Delhi Region candidates (qualifying exam passed from a recognised school/college in NCT of Delhi) and 15% to Outside Delhi candidates; for Patrachar Vidyalaya/NIOS the examination centre location decides.

NSUT, DTU, IGDTUW and DSEU need 60% or more aggregate in Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics, a pass in English, a JEE Main 2026 rank and a pass in every other subject; relaxed to OBC-NCL 55%, SC/ST 50%, Defence 55%, PwD 50%; no relaxation for EWS.

IIIT-Delhi needs 70% or more in the best five subjects including Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics, with 70% or more in Mathematics, plus JEE Main rank; relaxed to OBC-NCL 65%, SC/ST 60%, Defence 65%, PwD 65%; no EWS relaxation.
There is no minimum or maximum age criterion for any JAC Delhi institution; compartment cases of 2026 are not eligible in 2026.
2026 registration and choice filling ran 28 May to 9 June 2026, with a three-day extra window 26-28 June 2026; registration fee Rs 1,500; special spot round notices were issued in August 2026.

JoSAA (IITs, NITs, IIITs and GFTIs) requires Class 12 with PCM and at least 75% aggregate (65% for SC/ST/PwD) in five subjects, or being in the category-wise top 20 percentile of the board; this applies to JoSAA institutes, not to JAC Delhi seats at DTU/NSUT/IIIT-Delhi.
For JoSAA the home-state code follows the state of the Class 12 examination, not residence: a Delhi school student living in NOIDA is treated as Delhi.

Engineering needs Higher Secondary (Kerala or equivalent) with Physics and Mathematics compulsory and Chemistry as an optional subject; if Chemistry was not studied, Computer Science, else Biotechnology, else Biology marks are counted (clause 6.2.2).

General candidates need at least 45% marks put together in Physics, Mathematics and Chemistry (or the substitute subject) in the qualifying exam (clause 6.2.2); no separate minimum in Mathematics alone is stated.

SC/ST/SEBC and PD candidates need 40% instead of 45% in Physics, Mathematics and Chemistry/Computer Science/Biotechnology/Biology together; the SEBC relaxation also applies to OEC (clause 6.2.5(v) and note).
No separate marks relaxation for EWS in engineering is stated in the text read, so EWS is treated like General (45%); not confirmed as a distinct rule.
Percentages are not rounded: 135 out of 300 counts as 45%, anything lower does not (clause 6.2.8).

The engineering rank list gives equal 50:50 weightage to the normalized KEAM entrance score (out of 300) and the normalized final-year Class 12 marks in Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry combined 5:3:2 (150:90:60, out of 300), giving an index mark out of 600 (clause 9.7.4(b), per G.O.(Rt) No.1615/2025/HEDN dated 26.12.2025).

Each subject mark is normalized board-wise and year-wise using the highest mark scored by that board's students in that subject and year; for CBSE and CISCE the national-level highest mark is used (clause 9.7.4(b)(iii),(vii)).

To appear in the engineering rank list a candidate needs a minimum normalized score of 10 out of 300 in the KEAM engineering paper; SC/ST have no minimum but must answer at least one question (clause 9.7.5(i)).

Applicants must have completed 17 years on 31 December 2026 with no relaxation; no upper age limit for Engineering, Architecture, B.Pharm, BAMS, BSMS, BHMS, BUMS; MBBS/BDS upper age follows the NEET(UG)-2026 bulletin (clause 6.3.1).

Candidates are Keralite, Non-Keralite Category I (NK I, for example 5 years residence within 12 years of study, or school studies in Kerala from Std VIII to XII) or NK II; NK I compete for State Merit seats but get no communal, special or PD reservation or fee concession (clause 6.1).

NK II candidates are not eligible for Government colleges in medical, engineering, pharmacy or architecture, but may take Government cost-sharing engineering seats after the second phase if Keralites/NK I are unavailable, and private self-financing seats; 15% of MBBS, BAMS, BSMS, BUMS seats in self-financing colleges are open irrespective of domicile on the NEET-UG rank (clause 6.1(iii)).
B.Pharm needs 10+2 with English and Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics/Biology as optional subjects; no minimum percentage is stated (clause 6.2.4).

B.Pharm rank list is made from the Kerala Pharmacy Entrance Examination score with a minimum normalized score of 10 out of 300; SC/ST have no minimum but must answer at least one question (clauses 9.7.4(f), 9.7.5(v)).

B.Sc (Hons) Agriculture, Forestry, Co-operation & Banking/Agri Business Management, B.Tech Biotechnology (KAU) and BFSc need Physics, Chemistry and Biology with 50% put together (clause 6.2.1(v)); Climate Change & Environmental Science needs the same 50% PCB and Mathematics studied at Plus Two (clause 6.2.1(vi)).
For these courses SEBC and PD candidates need 5% less than General (45%); SC/ST need only a pass mark (clause 6.2.5(iii)).
BVSc & AH needs English, Physics, Chemistry and Biology passed with 50% aggregate; SC/ST/SEBC/PD need 47.5% (clauses 6.2.1(vii), 6.2.5(iv)).

MBBS/BDS need Physics, Chemistry, Biology/Biotechnology and English passed individually with at least 50% in Physics, Chemistry and Biology/Biotechnology together; SC/ST/SEBC and PD need 40% (clauses 6.2.1(i), 6.2.5(i)).

BAMS/BHMS/BSMS/BUMS need 10+2 with Physics, Chemistry and Biology/Biotechnology per AYUSH UG regulations; no percentage is stated; BSMS needs Tamil and BUMS Urdu/Arabic/Persian studied (clause 6.2.1(ii)-(iv)).

For MBBS/BDS/BAMS/BHMS/BSMS/BUMS the NEET-UG 2026 cut-off is the 50th percentile (SC/ST/SEBC 40th; PD 45th unreserved, 40th SC/ST/SEBC); for agriculture, forestry, veterinary and fisheries a minimum of 20 NEET marks, none for SC/ST (clause 9.7.5(ii),(iii)).

State-quota allotment to government and private self-financing MBBS/BDS (including NRI and minority seats) and to AYUSH colleges is done by common counselling conducted by the Commissioner for Entrance Examinations (CEE) on NEET-UG rank (clause 2.2, 9.7.4(d)).
This prospectus does not list B.Sc Nursing among KEAM courses; nursing admission route not confirmed.
KEAM 2026 engineering entrance was 13-25 April 2026, result on or before 10 May 2026, engineering and B.Pharm rank lists on or before 20 June 2026 (prospectus cover schedule).

AP EAPCET 2026 (Engineering) requires Intermediate (10+2) with Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry (or related vocational course) from the BIE Andhra Pradesh or equivalent, or a Diploma in Engineering; final-year appearing candidates may apply and the rank is valid only if they pass.
Candidates need at least 45% marks (40% for reserved category) in the subjects specified taken together in the qualifying examination; the booklet text does not give a separate PwD figure.
Ranks are computed 75% on AP EAPCET normalised marks and 25% on Intermediate marks in Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry (Engineering); the booklet says the normalisation procedure is under review.
The qualifying mark in AP EAPCET 2026 is 25% of the maximum marks considered for ranking; no minimum is prescribed for SC/ST, whose admission is limited to reserved seats.

For B.Tech Dairy Tech, Agr. Engg, Food Science & Tech and B.Sc Agr. Engg candidates must be 17 by 31 Dec 2026 with upper limit 22 years (25 for SC/ST); the booklet states no age rule for the main B.Tech engineering branches and Pharm.D needs 17 years by 31 Dec 2026.
AP EAPCET 2026 was held online 12-18 May 2026 (Engineering 12-15 and 18 May; Agriculture and Pharmacy 19-20 May); Engineering paper has 80 Maths, 40 Physics, 40 Chemistry questions.
AP EAPCET 2026 was conducted by JNTU Kakinada under APSCHE; the Commissioner of Technical Education, AP is the Convener for admissions.
The 2026 Engineering booklet does not mention JEE Main; admission to AP institutions under this booklet is through AP EAPCET rank (JEE Main role for AP institutes not confirmed).
Candidates must belong to Andhra Pradesh and satisfy local/non-local status as per Government of AP orders for 2026-27; booklet Annexure-III (definition) is an image and not machine-readable.

85% of seats are reserved for local candidates and 15% are unreserved (open to local and non-local); this G.O. is stated to apply to academic year 2025-26 only and the 2026-27 order was not confirmed.

Local to an area if studied there for at least 4 consecutive academic years ending with the year of first appearing in the qualifying exam (or resided 4 years if not studying); otherwise local to the area of longest study over 7 consecutive years.
AU area = erstwhile Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, East Godavari, West Godavari, Krishna, Guntur and Prakasam; SVU area = erstwhile Anantapur, Kurnool, Chittoor, Cuddapah and Nellore.

Unreserved 15% seats are open to those local in two areas, those resident 10 years in AP (or parent so), children of State/Central Govt or public-sector employees in AP, and spouses of such employees.

For B.Sc (Ag)/(Hort)/B.V.Sc/B.F.Sc, Intermediate with any two of Physical Science, Biological/Natural Science, Agriculture or the relevant vocational course; all must write Biology, Physics, Chemistry in the AP stream test.

B.Pharm (and B.Tech Bio-Technology) require Intermediate with Biology, Physics and Chemistry; B.Pharm minimum age 16 at admission with no upper limit; Pharm.D needs PCB or PCM (BiPC/MPC) with 17 years by 31 Dec 2026.
The same 45% (40% reserved category) minimum applies in the specified subjects, with a 75% EAPCET and 25% Intermediate rank weightage and 25% qualifying mark.
Notification 3 Feb 2026, applications from 4 Feb to 24 Mar 2026 (late fee to 10 Apr), AP stream exam 19-20 May 2026; no counselling dates and no 2027 dates were published on the dates page.
